description: Source code for the Twig Lexer class, responsible for tokenizing Twig templates, including handling of different states, regex patterns, and tokenization logic.

classes.name: Lexer
classes.description: A class that tokenizes Twig template source code into a stream of tokens, managing different parsing states and regex-based lexing.

methods.name: tokenize
methods.description: Main method to convert a Source object into a TokenStream by lexing the template code.

methods.name: initialize
methods.description: Initializes regex patterns and internal state for lexing, called once before tokenization.

methods.name: lexData
methods.description: Lexes plain text data outside of Twig tags, handling template text and tag detection.

methods.name: lexBlock
methods.description: Lexes content within block tags, handling end of block detection and expression lexing.

methods.name: lexVar
methods.description: Lexes content within variable tags, handling end detection and expression lexing.

methods.name: lexExpression
methods.description: Lexes expressions inside Twig tags, handling operators, names, numbers, strings, brackets, and comments.

methods.name: stripcslashes
methods.description: Processes escape sequences within string tokens, converting them to their actual characters.

methods.name: lexRawData
methods.description: Lexes raw data blocks like 'verbatim' sections, capturing unprocessed template text.

methods.name: lexComment
methods.description: Lexes and skips over comment blocks.

methods.name: lexString
methods.description: Lexes string tokens, including handling of interpolation and string delimiters.

methods.name: pushToken
methods.description: Adds a token to the token list, avoiding empty text tokens.

methods.name: moveCursor
methods.description: Advances the cursor position and line number based on processed text.

methods.name: getOperatorRegex
methods.description: Builds regex pattern for matching operators based on environment operators.

methods.name: pushState
methods.description: Saves current state and switches to a new lexing state.
